evidence.exact_quote: 5. **Disable and restore:** Bundled first-party specialty Personas can be disabled and restored to the shipped default after user customization. Protected core built-ins cannot be disabled. User-created and imported Personas can be deleted with confirmation.

items.impact: Concurrent editors, interrupted writes, restore failures, or deletion races can corrupt or silently overwrite a Persona because the contract defines user actions but no atomic commit, conflict, recovery, or rollback semantics.
items.statement: The Persona system specifies create, edit, disable, restore, and delete behavior but does not define atomic file mutation, optimistic concurrency, interruption recovery, or rollback guarantees.
items.title: Persona mutation lifecycle has no atomicity or recovery contract

evidence.exact_quote: `owner_hint` is advisory until resolved by the crew-role map. PM checks the active agent config `crew.roles` map, for example `{ "code-review": { provider, model, persona } }`, using exact tag matches such as `code-review`, `test-writer`, or `researcher`; partial matches are not supported in MVP. If no mapping exists, PM falls back to the current session provider/model while selecting the requested Persona behavior. If a mapping exists but the mapped provider or model is unavailable, PM returns `capability_unavailable` and does not silently fall back to a different provider/model/persona tuple.

items.impact: Callers cannot deterministically decide whether to prompt for an override, retry after configuration repair, remain blocked, or terminate, and support tooling lacks a required diagnostic payload.
items.statement: The crew-role mapping contract defines `capability_unavailable` as an outcome but omits its state transition, required diagnostic fields, retry or override path, and caller-visible recovery behavior.
items.title: Crew-role capability failure has no recovery protocol

evidence.exact_quote: A **Persona** is the assigned role definition that shapes an Agent's or Subagent's behavior. It is a static, declarative artifact — a YAML-frontmatter Markdown file — that acts as a **behavior-and-runtime contract**. In addition to identity, instructions, default permissions, and skill references, a Persona MAY declare provider/model/variant preferences, optional runtime control preferences, tool-usage guidance, aliases, and UI-facing metadata. When the Orchestrator or Interview phase manager selects a Persona for a run, the Persona's content and runtime metadata feed both the Agent's compiled context and the effective runtime resolution flow.

items.impact: Implementations have a clear distinction between persistent role artifacts, ephemeral execution units, child runs, and provider-native configuration.
items.statement: Agent, Subagent, Persona, and provider-native concepts are separated by identity, lifetime, authority, and storage boundaries.
items.title: Runtime and artifact identities are clearly separated

evidence.exact_quote: Core Persona default model/provider/runtime controls appear as Auto in the UI and are stored as inherited/null fields unless a PM-owned definition sets a value; core definitions are user-immutable, explorer and bash are subagent-only, assistant and teacher are direct user-facing Personas, and other protected core Personas are chat-selectable unless a narrower owner rule forbids the surface.

assistant is the default chat Persona with broad capability similar to general-purpose, a warmer and more collaborative style, permission to do real work when warranted, and boundaries against becoming a hidden worker Persona or passive help-bot.

items.impact: Picker eligibility, mutability, inherited controls, child selection recording, and broad assistant/general routing have a coherent baseline.
items.statement: The core catalog defines hierarchy, protected mutability, picker eligibility, inherited Auto controls, child selection recording, and distinct assistant/general behavior boundaries.
items.title: Core Persona catalog boundaries are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: explorer is a fast, read-only, subagent-only core Persona for codebase-local investigation that searches files, symbols, configs, tests, docs, and call sites, returns concise evidence-backed synthesis, and does not edit, refactor, implement, or use web research by default.

bash is a subagent-only terminal-execution Persona that runs useful command sequences in an isolated context, inspects stdout, stderr, exit status, and side effects, and reports the smallest actionable result without becoming a general planner or coding Persona.

researcher is a read-only Persona that combines local codebase inspection with current external sources when those sources materially improve the answer, stays grounded in project context, compares evidence, and returns citations plus handoff guidance without taking over implementation.

items.impact: Read-only Personas may still receive mutating tools or leak sensitive project context externally, while Bash can perform destructive side effects without a Persona-specific approval, rollback, or evidence requirement.
items.statement: Explorer and Researcher declare read-only behavior and Bash acknowledges side effects, but the units do not define enforceable tool capability sets, mutation classification, destructive-command approval, rollback evidence, external-source trust handling, secret redaction, citation failure, or project-data lifecycle rules.
items.title: Specialized core Personas lack enforceable hazard boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: overseer is a governance/conductor Persona, not the scheduler personified and not a normal node-worker implementation Persona; scheduler and executor owners retain dispatchability, readiness, transitions, blocked-state lifecycle, retries, wakeups, attempt identity, and hard Orchestrator mechanics.

overseer expresses delegation-first, verification-first, wiring/completeness-sensitive, integration-aware, audit-minded behavior; package-overseer mode governs package-local readiness and remediation evidence, while seam-overseer mode judges cross-package integration, wiring, architecture consistency, GUI/runtime fit, workflow completeness, weak integration, and coherent feature formation.

items.impact: Overseer can appear to decide readiness or cross-package completion without a machine-visible authority grant, and disagreements or failed handoffs can be buried or deadlock despite prose requiring visibility.
items.statement: Teacher and Overseer boundaries are directionally clear, but the package/seam authority token, direct-action authorization record, handoff acceptance, disagreement/corroboration state machine, timeout/escalation path, and user-visible blocked or incomplete states remain unspecified.
items.title: Overseer governance boundary lacks an executable handoff protocol

evidence.exact_quote: There is no protected core document-writer Persona; durable document creation is workflow behavior handled by the owning surface and resolved stage Persona, and generated requirements, summaries, plans, reports, and durable artifacts remain draft workflow outputs until accepted by the relevant user or validation gate.

items.impact: Consumers cannot reliably distinguish draft, submitted, rejected, superseded, accepted, or revoked artifacts, and a later failed validation may not have a defined rollback or provenance-preserving response.
items.statement: The document-generation boundary defines artifacts as draft until acceptance but does not define artifact identity, acceptance authority, submitted/rejected/superseded states, validation failure handling, version lineage, revocation, or rollback after acceptance.
items.title: Draft document outputs have no complete acceptance lifecycle

segments.summary: Reviewed the canonical Persona definitions, storage, schema, GUI, selection, and integration prologue; the dominant adversarial gap is the absence of atomic mutation and recovery semantics across GUI-managed file operations.

Reviewed acceptance criteria, runtime expansion, core and specialty catalog prose, owner map, and P-002/P-003; SSOT ownership is strong, P-003 is misclassified as GUI work, and crew-role capability failure lacks a recovery protocol.
Reviewed P-004 through P-011; identity boundaries are clear, while PERSONA.md path/parser trust and runtime-control value domains remain underspecified.
Reviewed P-012 through P-019; body injection is explicit, but the Persona GUI lacks adversarial accessibility and transaction states and child capability reduction is not executable.
Reviewed P-020 through P-027; cross-subsystem ownership is enumerated but lacks an end-to-end consumer oracle, and product acceptance criteria are connected only to plan validators.
Reviewed P-028 through P-035; core catalog boundaries are coherent, but GUI persistence and runtime resolution lack transactional stability and recovery detail.

Reviewed P-036 through P-043; specialized Personas lack enforceable hazard boundaries, Overseer lacks an executable authority and handoff protocol, and durable draft artifacts lack a complete acceptance lifecycle.
